Dancing with the Stars employs a 50/50 scoring system, equally weighted between the judges' scores and the audience vote.

The regular judging panel consists of Derek Hough, Carrie Ann Inaba, and Bruno Tonioli, who are joined by a weekly guest judge. Each of the four judges scores every performance on a scale of 1 to 10. The couple's total judge scores are converted into a percentage based on the cumulative points awarded by all judges throughout the night.

Audience votes received by a couple are converted into a percentage based on the night's total audience vote count (the "Public Vote Percentage"). The Judge's Score Percentage and the Public Vote Percentage are then added together to determine each couple's final ranking for the week.

- Online: Via the official ABC website
- Text Message: By sending a specific text code for their favorite couple, as specified during the broadcast.
Viewers are allowed to cast up to 10 votes per couple, with a maximum of 20 total votes per viewer each week.

articles.headline: Longtime Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford dies at age 101
keyFacts: Martha Firestone Ford, the longtime primary owner of the Detroit Lions, died at age 101 at her home, the team announced.
Ford and her husband purchased the team in 1963, and she took over controlling interest after his death in 2014 before passing it to her daughter in 2020.
No cause of death was given by the team, though officials stated she was surrounded by her family.
body: Martha Firestone Ford, who served as the primary owner of the Detroit Lions from 2014 to 2020, has died at the age of 101, the team announced Tuesday night.

"Over more than six decades with the Detroit Lions, she was a loyal and constant fixture of the franchise, sharing in its history and traditions," the team said in a statement announcing her death. "She remained present with the team even this season, attending games with a devotion that endured throughout her life."
No cause of death was given, although the team said she died at home surrounded by her family.
Ford and her husband, William Clay Ford Sr., bought the Lions in 1963, and she took over his controlling interest in the team after his death in 2014.

Although she seldom spoke to reporters or commented publicly on the direction of the franchise, her influence was felt. She was in charge of the team from 2014 until 2020, when she turned the Lions over to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp.
Ford had since served as chair emeritus.

The Lions made the playoffs in 2014 but lost seven of their first eight games the following season. In November 2015, the team fired its president and general manager in a midseason shakeup. When she announced the changes, Ford told fans the franchise intended to "identify and hire the very best leadership in order to produce a consistently, winning football team."
The Lions played better down the stretch that season, and after hiring Bob Quinn as their new general manager, they returned to the playoffs a year later.

Although Ford kept a low profile, the shakeup in the middle of the 2015 season was a sign that she was more than willing to bring about change in an effort to reverse the team's fortunes. Then-coach Jim Caldwell said she was very much a presence within the organization.

"I think visible ownership is great, and Mrs. Ford does it extremely well," Caldwell said in 2015. "She's there before games and she's there after games, and I think guys enjoy that part of it. She comes to practice and things of that nature, so it's been fun."

Ford also made an impact in the Detroit community. She was an officer on the board for Detroit Lions Charities and on the board of the Henry Ford Health System. Martha and William Clay Ford were credited with helping establish the Maplegrove Center, a substance abuse treatment facility in West Bloomfield.

Born Sept. 16, 1925, in Akron, Ohio, Martha Parke Firestone was a granddaughter of tire magnate Harvey Firestone. She graduated from Vassar College in 1946 and married William Clay Ford Sr., Henry Ford's grandson, the next year.
In 2017, Forbes estimated her net worth at more than $1.4 billion. She is survived by her four children, 14 grandchildren and 17 great-grandchildren.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Who's on the CFP bubble after the committee's fourth ranking?
keyFacts: Indiana dropped to No. 14 in the selection committee's fourth ranking, threatening its College Football Playoff chances.
The committee moved Tennessee to No. 5 and Alabama to No. 6, honoring Tennessee's head-to-head victory over the Tide.
With one regular-season game remaining, several bubble teams across multiple conferences remain in contention for the playoff.
body: The defending national champs are in danger of missing the College Football Playoff after two-loss Indiana sank to No. 14 in the selection committee's fourth ranking of the season.

While the Hoosiers' significant slide was the most impactful move of the night, it was hardly the only one that shook up the playoff picture, as the committee reset the SEC order and finally honored Tennessee's head-to-head win against Alabama, moving the Vols to No. 5 followed by the Tide at No. 6.
No. 3 Texas is now the committee's top two-loss team.

And yet there's still so much that can change with just one game remaining in the regular season. No school has clinched a spot in the Big Ten championship game, but No. 9 UCLA, No. 12 Oregon, No. 13 Iowa and No. 14 Indiana still can. How realistic are the playoff chances for the Big Ten schools that don't win the league?
Bubble Watch is your guide to answering that question.

Below, you'll find teams with "would be in" status. Those are the schools in this week's bracket based on Tuesday night's ranking. For each Power 4 conference, we've also listed "last team in" and "first team out." These are the true bubble teams hovering around inclusion. Teams labeled "still in the mix" haven't been eliminated but have work to do. A team that is "out" will have to wait until next season.
The conferences below are listed in order of the number of bids they'd receive, ranked from the most to least, based on the latest CFP top 25.
Jump to a conference:
ACC | Big 12 | Big Ten
SEC | Independent | Group of 6
Bracket
SEC
Would be in: Georgia, Texas, Tennessee, Alabama

Last team in: Alabama (9-2). With UCLA losing and dropping below Wake Forest, the committee had a chance to compare Tennessee and Alabama in the same voting pool. With the same record and similar schedule metrics, the committee now deems those teams comparable and honored the Vols' 26-10 win over the Tide on Oct. 17. No. 5 Tennessee and No. 6 Alabama are in spots to host first-round CFP games, awarded to seed Nos. 5-8. Alabama's win against Chattanooga of the FCS coupled with the fact that some of its opponents once regarded as its best wins continued to lose (South Carolina, Kentucky and LSU) contributed to its drop. The Tide are still ranked in the top seven of ESPN's strength of record and strength of schedule metrics.
First team out: None. After the aforementioned top four, every other team in the SEC has at least four losses.

Still in the mix: None. Georgia, Texas, Tennessee and Alabama all have at least an 89% chance to reach the playoff, but every other team in the league is at less than 1%, according to the Allstate Playoff Predictor.
Out: Arkansas, Auburn, Florida, Kentucky, LSU, Mississippi State, Missouri, Oklahoma, Ole Miss, South Carolina, Texas A&M, Vanderbilt
ACC
Would be in: Miami, Wake Forest

Last team in: Wake Forest (10-1). The Deacs have locked up a spot in the ACC championship game and were bumped up to No. 8 after their convincing win against Georgia Tech and UCLA's loss at Michigan. As long as Wake Forest avoids an upset to Duke on Saturday in the regular-season finale, it should finish among the top 12, even with a loss to Miami in the ACC title game. The Deacs have a 67.1% chance to reach the CFP and a 77.6% chance to beat Duke on Saturday. ESPN's FPI gives Miami a 61.9% chance to win the ACC title.
First team out: None. There aren't any other ACC teams within range of cracking the top 12, even with multiple upsets.
Still in the mix: None. No. 19 Louisville is the only three-loss team remaining, as Clemson, SMU and Duke each have four losses, and every other team in the league has at least five.
Out: Boston College, Cal, Clemson, Duke, Florida State, Georgia Tech, Louisville, North Carolina, NC State, Pitt, SMU, Stanford, Syracuse, Virginia, Virginia Tech
Big 12
Would be in: Utah, BYU, Texas Tech

Last team in: Texas Tech (10-1). The Red Raiders have the second-best chance to reach the Big 12 championship game (83.8%) behind Utah, which already clinched a spot. If Texas Tech finishes as the league runner-up, it might miss the field, depending on what happens around the Red Raiders. They are No. 53 in offensive efficiency but No. 10 in ESPN's strength of record metric. If Texas Tech beats Utah, and the Utes finish with one loss and BYU holds steady at No. 10, the Big 12 could get all three teams in.
First team out: None. None. No. 16 Arizona is the next-highest ranked Big 12 team and has less than a 1% chance to reach the CFP, according to the Allstate Playoff Predictor.
Still in the mix: None. Every other team has at least three losses, and none has a strong case for inclusion.
Out: Arizona, Arizona State, Baylor, Cincinnati, Colorado, Houston, Iowa State, Kansas, Kansas State, Oklahoma State, TCU, UCF, West Virginia
Big Ten
Would be in: UCLA

Last team in: UCLA (10-1). The Bruins dropped to No. 9 following their loss to Michigan but still have a 59% chance to make the Big Ten title game -- second only to No. 13 Oregon (86.5%). The Bruins host rival USC on Saturday, and ESPN's FPI gives them a 50.8% chance to win. If UCLA beats USC and faces Oregon for the second time this season and loses, the Bruins would be able to claim a regular-season win against the eventual Big Ten champs. UCLA beat the Ducks 17-15 on Oct. 10. That could factor into how far the committee might drop them as the Big Ten runner-up.

First team out: Oregon (8-3). The Ducks have a 61.9% chance of reaching the CFP, according to the Allstate Playoff Predictor, and an 86.5% chance of reaching the Big Ten championship game. No team in the Big Ten has higher chances of reaching the CFP or winning the conference title (57.8%). According to ESPN Research, Oregon can clinch a spot in the Big Ten title game Saturday with a win against Washington and an Iowa loss; or a win and a UCLA win; or a win and an Indiana win.

Still in the mix: Iowa (9-2), Indiana (9-2). The two-loss Hawkeyes are here because there are still multiple (albeit convoluted) ways they can reach the Big Ten championship game. Iowa has the fourth-best chance to do that (24.3%) behind Oregon, UCLA and Indiana. The Hawkeyes have a 34.2% chance to reach the CFP. No. 14 Indiana is still in the mix because it can technically still reach the Big Ten title game, though it needs a lot of help. The Hoosiers have a 29.6% chance of reaching the Big Ten championship, slightly ahead of Iowa.
Out: Illinois, Maryland, Michigan, Michigan State, Minnesota, Nebraska, Northwestern, Ohio State, Penn State, Purdue, Rutgers, USC, Washington, Wisconsin
Independent

Would be in: Notre Dame (10-1). No. 4 Notre Dame bumped into first-round bye territory. The Irish are No. 5 in ESPN's strength of record metric, with their win against Miami highlighting their résumé and helping to offset a close loss at BYU on Oct. 17. Notre Dame's strength of schedule is No. 51, though, which trails Alabama (No. 18) and Texas (No. 6). Notre Dame's win against Miami is its only victory against a CFP top-25 opponent. Notre Dame will lock up a spot in the playoff race with a win Saturday at Syracuse. Notre Dame is in the top five in offensive and defensive efficiency.
Group of 6

Would be in: Boise State (9-2). Boise State fell out of the committee's top 25, but even after its second loss of the season, Boise State still has the best chance of any Group of 6 team to reach the playoff at 36.8%, according to ESPN Analytics. The Broncos lead the pack with the No. 26 strength of record, and their strength of schedule is No. 80, which is slightly better than UTSA (No. 82) and Louisiana Tech (No. 87), and significantly above Liberty (No. 135). Boise State has already clinched a spot in the Pac-12 title game, but it can't afford to stumble again. The Broncos will travel to Colorado State for their regular-season finale before facing San Diego State on Dec. 4 in the Pac-12 championship. ESPN's FPI gives Boise State at least an 89% chance to win each of those games.

Still in the mix: Liberty (10-1), Louisiana Tech (9-2), UTSA (9-2), New Mexico (9-2). If Boise State loses, the door opens for one of these teams. Liberty has the second-best chance to reach the playoff behind Boise State at 28.6%, followed by Louisiana Tech at 15.8% and UTSA at 15.2%. Liberty is the only one-loss team in the group, and it lost to James Madison in the Sept. 5 season opener. The selection committee is more likely to put a two-loss Boise State in than it is to reward a one-loss team with the No. 135-ranked schedule.

articles.headline: U.S. Spying Agencies Reportedly Hacked
keyFacts: U.S. officials and sources told The New York Times that several U.S. spying agencies were believed breached, exposing non-classified data.
Sources suggested that China may be behind the attack using an artificial intelligence tool, and stated the breach has been resolved.
A separate report by The Verge stated the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network was also breached in a potentially unrelated event.
body: An anonymously-sourced New York Times report on Tuesday says the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) along with the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (part of the Pentagon) and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence are believed to have been breached by attackers in an operation believed to have exposed non-classified data.
The Times cites “U.S. officials and other people familiar with the matter.” One of these anonymous sources told the Times the breach has been resolved.

Some of the Times’ sources point to the AI harness Artexâa Chinese tool theoretically intended for white-hat hackingâas the attackers’ apparent secret weapon, and “suggest that China may be behind” the breach.
An additional Tuesday report from the Verge says the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), part of the Treasury Department, was also breached in what may be a completely separate event.

The somewhat cagey New York Times report says an unnamed network that pulls “intelligence insights” from publicly accessible records was targeted, but it’s not clear what kind of open-source data may now be compromised, if any.

Open source intelligence (OSINT) is a broad term that includes many types of publicly available information that can be used for things like targeting of military strikes. One report from last year suggested that the Pentagon may have been pulling targeting information from questionable X postsâjust one example of potential open-source intelligence.

articles.headline: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
keyFacts: A US jury found Huawei guilty of trade secret theft and bank fraud, but acquitted the firm of racketeering charges.
Prosecutors accused Huawei of using theft to gain a competitive edge, but Huawei argued its success stemmed from innovation.
Huawei's sentencing is scheduled for September 2027, and the company's defense attorney expects Huawei to appeal the verdict.
body: - Published
Huawei has been found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but not guilty of the more serious overarching racketeering charge in a landmark case in the US.
In a two-month trial, prosecutors accused the Chinese technology and telecommunications giant of lying, cheating and stealing to gain any competitive advantage.
Huawei's defence team argued that prosecutors had decided Huawei was a criminal organisation and built its case from there, but the firm's success was due to its own innovation.
Huawei said, external the racketeering acquittal "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis", adding that it would "take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests".
Jurors in a Brooklyn court found Huawei guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, which included conspiracy to violate US sanctions.
However, the jury declined to convict Huawei of the racketeering conspiracy charge, which required members to find the firm acted like a criminal enterprise.
Federal prosecutors first announced the charges against Huawei in 2019, after the dramatic arrest in late 2018 of senior executive Meng Wanzhou in Canada.
Meng, also known as Cathy Meng, was held for three years in Canada before she was released to return to China through a deal with US prosecutors.

During closing arguments last week, assistant US attorney Meredith Arfa told jurors Huawei spent 20 years doing whatever it took to expand its business, including lying to banks about its business dealings in Iran and stealing technology secrets from rival firms to ensure it had a competitive edge.
"For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in statement, external.
"Thanks to the work of the FBI and our federal prosecutors, those who engaged in these criminal activities will be held accountable."
However, defence attorney Brian Heberlig said it was by dint of hard work that Huawei's business had expanded with operations in 170 countries and more than 200,000 staff.
Following the verdict, Heberlig told the BBC that Huawei was gratified that the jury had rejected the racketeering charge.

"The RICO [Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations Act] count that alleged that Huawei was a corrupt organisation, with a corporate culture and policy of committing crime. That was, in our view, a significant overreach, and the jury soundly rejected it," he said.
"Of course, we have mixed emotions about the rest of the verdict ... [we] thought that Huawei was deserving of acquittals across the board."
Sentencing is planned for September 2027. Heberlig said there will be "significant advocacy" to achieve the lowest sentence possible. Following that, he said he fully expects Huawei to appeal.
"If I know Huawei, that fight will continue, and the company's not going to rest until it's pursued every last argument it can through appeal, and hopefully, ultimately toward vindication," he said.

articles.headline: China launches Shenzhou-24 to Tiangong station
keyFacts: China launched the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft with three crew members to the Tiangong space station, according to the China Manned Space Agency.
The crew includes Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who is the first foreign astronaut to fly on a Chinese crewed space mission.
The astronauts will conduct over 90 experiments, and astronaut Zhu Yangzhu will begin a full-year stay on the space station.
body: The Shenzhou-24 spacecraft lifted off on a Long March-2F rocket at 8:18 am local time (0018 GMT) from the Jiuquan launch center in the Gobi Desert.
The China Manned Space Agency reported that the capsule separated from the rocket about 10 minutes later and entered orbit, and called the launch a "complete success".
State broadcaster CCTV showed the three crew members leafing through a manual minutes after liftoff and reported that they were in good condition.
What do we know about the crew?

Tang Hongbo is making his third trip to space. CCTV said he will become the first astronaut to board Tiangong three times. Wu Yi is on his first flight, as is Pakistani pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreigner to fly on a Chinese crewed mission.
"I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis," Ali told a news conference on Tuesday, switching between Urdu, Mandarin and English.

The handover on the station will be unusual. Shenzhou-23 commander Zhu Yangzhu will remain on board for a year, while the rest of his crew — Lai Ka-ying, Hong Kong's first astronaut, and Zhang Zhiyuan — return to Earth with Ali.

Zhu's stay is reportedly China's first full-year spell in space. Reuters said it will be the longest single stay by a Chinese astronaut. It has been described as a test of how the human body copes, ahead of planned Moon missions and possibly a journey to Mars.
What is on the agenda?

The crew will carry out more than 90 experiments and technology tests, Xinhua reported. At a news conference on Tuesday, Tang said differences in language, culture and psychology had made teamwork harder, but that both sides' efforts were paying off.
Ali, speaking in Mandarin, told reporters: "It's like my daily training. Day after day, reaching new heights."
China's 2030 target for a crewed Moon landing is unchanged despite the delay to its Chang'e-7 lunar mission. The United States is aiming for 2028.

articles.headline: Nearly 6 decades after teen was killed while leaving job, Canada authorities know who did it
keyFacts: London police identified Michael Joseph Moore as responsible for the 1968 killing of 16-year-old Jacqueline Dunleavy.
Officials said Moore, who died in 2018, was identified through genetic genealogy.
Dunleavy's family expressed hope that the techniques used to solve her death can be used with other cold cases.
body: Authorities in Canada have identified a man accused of killing a Canadian teen nearly six decades ago, police said Monday.
Michael Joseph Moore, who died in 2018, was responsible for the 1968 death of Jacqueline “Jacky” Dunleavy, 16, according to the London Police Service in Ontario.

Moore, who worked as a firefighter for nearly three decades, was identified through genetic genealogy, officials said at a news conference Monday. The forensic technique combines modern DNA analysis with traditional genealogical research.
If Moore was alive today, the agency said in a statement, he would have been arrested and charged in connection with the teen’s death.
“Publicly identifying Moore provides an accurate historical record and answers that Jackie’s family and the community have sought for decades,” the agency said.
In a statement read at the news conference, Dunleavy’s family thanked law enforcement and said they hope the techniques used to solve her death can be used with other cold cases.
Authorities did not identify a possible motive, and a possible connection between Moore and Dunleavy remained unclear.

The high school sophomore was last seen on the evening of Jan. 9, 1968, leaving her job at a variety store in London, roughly 120 miles northeast of Detroit. Dunleavy was found dead at a school 90 minutes later, the police service said.
She had a head injury, according to the authorities, and her cause of death was determined to be strangulation.
More cold case coverage
- A dead homeless man was known as ‘Box Mike’ — until a global search revealed his true identity
- Chicago police find killer in 65-year-old cold case murder of little girl — one of their own
- Arrest made in cold case of Iowa real estate agent killed during an open house
- After 40 years and 3 overturned convictions, arrest made in murder case thanks to smoothie straw
- Slaying suspect in San Diego charged with 3 more murders, including 2 cold cases
Despite what the agency described as an extensive investigation, the case remained unsolved, and efforts in the decades that followed did not reveal her killer.

“The investigators who worked on Jackie’s homicide in 1968 did everything they could with the investigative and forensic tools available to them at the time,” Det. Sgt. Micah Bourdeau of the London Police Service said in a statement. “The evidence they carefully collected and preserved ultimately allowed investigators decades later to continue that work.”
Recently, a Texas-based DNA lab conducted specialized testing using that evidence and investigators were able to develop a family tree that helped identify Moore, the police service said.
After conducting additional interviews, gathering new evidence and obtaining comparison DNA samples, Moore was identified as the man responsible for the teen’s killing, the agency said.

Moore, who was 25 at the time, had moved to Canada from Ireland in 1967, authorities said. He worked as a firefighter for 28 years but did not have that job until after Dunleavy’s death, Det. Mike Budzyn of the London Police Service told reporters.
At the time he retired, Moore was a captain.
His family was shocked by the revelation, Budzyn said, and “expressed their hope that these findings will provide long-awaited answers for Jackie’s family.”

articles.headline: Kari Lake says she hasn’t given ‘even one minute of thought’ to 2028 amid Iowa bid speculation
keyFacts: Kari Lake stated she has not given the 2028 election thought amid speculation about a potential political campaign in Iowa.
President Donald Trump nominated Lake for an ambassadorship in Jamaica while she serves at the U.S. Agency for Global Media.
Her ambassadorship nomination will lapse at the end of the year unless congressional leadership provides dedicated Senate floor time.
body: EXCLUSIVE — Kari Lake , the Trump ally nominated to an ambassadorship in Jamaica, says she has “not given the 2028 election even one minute of thought” amid speculation that she will run for political office in her home state of Iowa .
In a text message, Lake told the Washington Examiner that she’s focused on the “here and now” and continues to serve in the Trump administration as deputy CEO of the U.S. Agency for Global Media.

Her statement follows a Tuesday report from the Arizona Republic questioning her employment there and whether her purchase of a condo in Iowa last year is a sign that she’s laying the groundwork for a 2028 campaign in the state.
If Lake does run for political office in Iowa, she may decide to pursue the seat of Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-IA), who at 93 has yet to say whether he will run for a ninth Senate term in 2028.

Lake, a former TV newscaster and MAGA firebrand who unsuccessfully ran for governor and Senate in Arizona, was chosen for an ambassadorship after a federal judge voided her attempts to fire hundreds of employees at the U.S. Agency for Global Media, a conglomerate of government news networks.

She initially joined the agency as deputy CEO but took on the responsibilities of acting CEO last year without Senate confirmation, a step the judge said was “unlawful.” On Tuesday, Lake said that she’s still “working to effectuate the President’s executive order to reduce the agency’s footprint to what is statutorily required.”

Her ambassador nomination made it through the Senate Foreign Relations Committee a month after President Donald Trump chose her for the post in May, but it’s one of several facing opposition from Republican holdouts and will lapse at the end of the year unless congressional leadership gives it dedicated floor time.

Lake, when asked about her condo purchase in January, said that she was focused on her “mission to help President Trump Make America Great Again” but did not close the door on another campaign, stating that she “loves” Iowa.
CHUCK GRASSLEY, 93, WON’T STEP DOWN EARLY AFTER DEMOCRAT ROB SAND WINS IOWA GOVERNORSHIP
“It’s where I was raised, where I went to college, and where so much of my story began,” Lake said . “Expanding our roots there means being closer to family and closer to the values that shaped me.”
She’s drawn similar speculation with her more frequent posting about University of Iowa football on social media.

articles.headline: CFP selection committee finally gets it right with Tennessee, Indiana rankings
keyFacts: The College Football Playoff selection committee released rankings that emphasized resumes and metrics by lowering Alabama and moving Texas to No. 3.
Tennessee secured the No. 5 spot in prime position to host a playoff game, while Indiana dropped six spots to No. 14.
Indiana's playoff hopes now heavily rely on making and winning the Big Ten Championship following the recent rankings drop.
body: The College Football Playoff selection committee finally did it.

For the first time this season, the rankings…made sense. I wasn't filled with confusion and frustration over what the committee decided. Instead, the committee made decisions that seemed to emphasize resumes and metrics over ambiguous "eye test" considerations.
Consider the big moves from this week:

The committee finally ended its love affair with Alabama and moved the Crimson Tide three spots. It would have made sense to do so a week ago but credit the committee for acknowledging that Alabama's resume has taken a significant hit over the last month. With Kentucky and South Carolina dropping out of this week's rankings, Alabama is without a top-25 win and will presumably end its season without one against unranked Auburn in the Iron Bowl.

With that move, the committee moved Texas to No. 3 () as the best two-loss team in the country. If Texas makes it to the SEC Championship and beats Georgia, it is an absolute lock for a top-four seed and first-round bye. Even if it loses to Georgia in the SEC title game, there's still a possibility it could finish in the top four depending on what happens elsewhere.

- Tennessee may not ever rank higher than its No. 5 spot Tuesday night, but it puts the Volunteers in prime position to host a playoff game. Earlier this week I called Neyland Stadium the greatest home-field advantage in college football, and it'd be a massive boon for the Vols to get one in Knoxville. There may not be a more ecstatic fanbase than Tennessee this week, after decrying Alabama's spot above the Volunteers for weeks. Mercifully for all of us, we won't have to discuss pods and groupings and whether head-to-head will be considered as much anymore with Alabama and Tennessee.

- Wake Forest is perhaps the hottest team in the country, and the committee has finally taken notice. The Demon Deacons jumped up to No. 8 from No. 10 a week ago. If those rankings hold for championship weekend, we'll get a No. 7 Miami versus No. 8 Wake Forest ACC Championship. Wake Forest is demolishing opponents and has the potential to keep moving up the rankings if it can win out. Conversely, Miami still has a chance to jump into that top four and get a bye as ACC champion. It would give the Hurricanes two wins over a very good Wake Forest team this season, and its lone loss coming to No. 4 Notre Dame.

- Indiana is not a playoff-caliber team at the moment, and the committee reflected that in the Hoosiers' six-spot drop. Was that too far a drop? Potentially. I predicted Indiana to land at No. 12 as the first team out rather than at No. 14 behind both Oregon and Iowa. Indiana has more top-25 wins and a better strength of schedule and strength of record than Iowa. The Hoosiers have a legitimate argument for being a spot too low. But I like the decision to rank Oregon, a team playing better football right now, above Indiana, especially with metrics like top-25 wins and strength of schedule to back up the decision.

What does it mean for Indiana now? The Hoosiers' playoff hopes may heavily rely on not only making the Big Ten Championship but winning it. As it stands right now, if UCLA (vs. USC) and Oregon (vs. Washington) both win this weekend, the Hoosiers will be out of luck. And with a No. 14 ranking and only a potential win over Purdue left on the schedule, I don't see a particularly realistic path into the playoff field. It'd be a stunning miss for last year's national championship team. And, yet, after an egregiously bad non-conference schedule, it is perhaps deserved.

Indiana's drop also increases the possibility of only one Big Ten team making the field. If UCLA, which dropped to No. 9 this week, loses to USC, the Bruins are out. Utah losing in the Big 12 title game could set up a scenario where three Big 12 teams make it (BYU and Texas Tech the others), four SEC teams make it, two ACC, Notre Dame, a Group of Six and then one of Oregon/Iowa/Indiana. The Big Ten bubble teams all need to be rooting for Utah to keep winning out and for BYU or Texas Tech to drop another game this weekend.

- I like how the committee handled the bottom of the top 25, too. Boise State missing the cut was a slight surprise but speaks to how much the Broncos' margin for error narrowed after a loss to San Diego State. Boise State still should be in if it wins out. After lots of public criticism over the number of four-loss SEC teams a week ago, the committee included a pair of Big Ten teams, Washington and Nebraska, that scored big wins last weekend. Washington and Nebraska are both deserving of spots 24 and 25. Ohio State's drop to No 21 feels fair, as well, given the Buckeyes' wins over Indiana and Iowa.

It's easy to criticize the selection committee each week for failing at an impossible task of ranking the top 25 teams. In fact, this space is usually reserved for pointing out the teams that the committee either over- or under-rated.
But if we're quick to criticize, we should also commend when appropriate. For one week, at least, this committee got it right.

articles.headline: Nvidia Is Also Trying to Fix the Bug Causing Excessive SSD Writing
keyFacts: A software bug in Nvidia graphics drivers has caused excessive data writing to solid-state drives for some users.
Nvidia acknowledged the issue in a software update after users reported up to 70GB of data per hour written to their drives.
Affected users are advised by experts to update immediately to Nvidia's latest drivers to install the fix.
body: Nvidia has had its share of drama lately, with the ousting and sudden un-ousting of CEO Jensen Huang after it was discovered he’d had multiple affairs, including one that involved an alleged member of a Chinese spy network. The fallout from the revelations was so significant that some worried Huang’s fate could be a major disruptor to the health of international markets and the future of the entire AI industry.

Given that, the world’s largest semiconductor company possibly wishes its biggest problem were software-related. But that won’t be much comfort to PC users affected by a software bug in Nvidia’s graphics driver that has caused some to experience excessive writes to their solid-state drives.

The issue began popping up in mid-November as posts on Nvidia’s support forums, as well as on Reddit and sites like HardForum, reported seeing as much as 30GB to 70GB of data per hour written to their SSDs. These types of drives wear down quickly over months of such use.
More from CNET

Nvidia didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment and hasn’t made any public statements on the issue, but did acknowledge it in a hotfix and subsequent software update for its Windows 11 GeForce Game Ready Driver 621.40, where it said under Fixed General Bugs, “Excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background.” The driver that appeared to have caused the problems was released on Nov. 12.

Some tech experts on social media had been suggesting rolling back to older graphics drivers before the hotfixes were released and warned that letting the problem go unchecked could cause an SSD to eventually fail.
Described by WCCF Tech as “a hotfix for the hotfix,” the new update appears to fix the issue in ways that the previous fix did not.

Nvidia’s software problem closely mirrors an issue AMD had with its own Adrenalin Edition graphics software just weeks ago. As of Nov. 18, AMD was still making tweaks to its graphics software to iron out any lingering problems.
What to check if you’re still concerned
PCGamer offered a way to check if your PC is affected by the excess writing issue.

Open Task Manager, click on the Details tab and right-click on the columns at the top to select “I/O write bytes” as one of your Task Manager columns. By doing that, you can see if the file “NVDisplay.Container.exe” is writing a huge amount of data to your data drive.

If that’s the case, you should update immediately to Nvidia’s latest drivers for the fix. In fact, it might be a good idea to update whether you’re experiencing high write rates or not, just to be safe.

articles.headline: NTSB chief presses for safety fixes before Army resumes flights near DCA
keyFacts: National Transportation Safety Board Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy stated Tuesday that the Army must implement safety recommendations before resuming helicopter training flights near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.
Homendy reported that only three of the 50 safety recommendations issued after a January 2025 midair collision have been addressed, leaving 47 open.
Representative Don Beyer also raised concerns regarding the Army's reported plans to resume helicopter training near the airport.
body: National Transportation Safety Board Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy on Tuesday said the Army must implement its safety recommendations before resuming helicopter training flights near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport .

Homendy’s urging follows a report revealing that the Pentagon plans to resume practice flights in the Washington, D.C. , airspace, which were suspended following a midair collision between an Army Black Hawk helicopter and an American Airlines flight in January 2025 that left 67 people dead. The chairwoman said in a statement that the team that investigated the collision was briefed on the decision.

“Members of the investigative team and I were briefed on the Army’s plans to begin the initial phase of a return to helicopter flights to the Pentagon through airspace near DCA as soon as December 1st,” Homendy said. “It is our understanding that the FAA has yet to receive a formal request for these flights. We have not seen the Army’s concept of operations and look forward to reviewing it once it is formally submitted to the FAA for evaluation.”

While the final decision on resuming training flights lies with the Federal Aviation Administration , the safety board issued 50 safety recommendations following its investigation into the DCA collision, which included overhauling helicopter routes and air traffic control procedures to improve separation and manage traffic capacity. Homendy said only three of those recommendations have seen action.

“What we will not lose sight of is the urgent need for action on the 47 open safety recommendations from our investigation into the midair collision near DCA, including recommendations to the Department of War on ADS-B Out and ADS-B In with a cockpit display of traffic information that is configured to provide alerting that is audible to the flight crew,” Homendy said, referring to satellite-based aircraft tracking technology.
Homendy also placed pressure on Congress , urging lawmakers to work on legislation that will close gaps in safety measures.

“This effort underscores the need for Congress to move forward with bipartisan, bicameral legislation that addresses the serious safety vulnerabilities identified in our investigation,” she said. “It’s been nearly two years since that tragedy. The flying public has waited long enough. We know what needs to be done to improve safety. The time to act is now.”

After the NTSB released Homendy’s statement, she took to X to “double down” on her calls for legislation, calling on the House Transportation and Infrastructure and Armed Services committees, as well as the Senate Armed Services and Commerce committees to take action.

“The House T&I, Senate Commerce, House Armed Services and Senate Armed Services Committees need to come together and finalize bipartisan legislation that addresses the significant safety concerns identified in our investigation, and ensures that all airspace users are held to the same high safety standards throughout the National Airspace System regardless of operation,” she said. “We have long held, one level of safety for all.”
DON BEYER RAISES ‘GRAVE CONCERNS’ OVER RESUMING ARMY TRAINING FLIGHTS NEAR RONALD REAGAN NATIONAL AIRPORT

Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA), who does not sit on the aforementioned committees but whose district includes DCA, echoed the NTSB’s concerns about the Army’s implementation of safety measures following reports of plans to return to helicopter training near the airport.
Beyer said he was briefed by Army officials who said a request was sent to the FAA to resume helicopter training.

articles.headline: Trump declares he’s ‘certainly not corrupt’ and hits out at ‘real’ grift in Minnesota, other Dem states

body: WASHINGTON — President Trump declared Tuesday that “I am certainly not corrupt” — as Democrats in Congress prepare for investigations to try to show that he is.

“I was of the impression when they said corruption, that they were talking about the corruption in Minnesota and California and Maine and all those, because that’s really the corruption,” he said in an Oval Office interview with The Post.
“I am certainly not corrupt. I don’t even — I have nothing to do with my stock portfolio. My son runs it, and I don’t even know what my stocks are.”

Democrats have forecast plans to place particular emphasis on investigating Trump’s cryptocurrency empire, which his financial disclosures said earned him $1.4 billion last year, as well as various other enterprises tied to his family and the relatives of senior officials.

Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.), the incoming chairman of the House Oversight Committee, said last week that his panel would be “fighting to put an end to this Administration’s self-dealing, misconduct, and abuse.”

The emergence of such evidence could make Trump’s remark to The Post an echo of President Richard Nixon’s famous line: “I’m not a crook.”

articles.headline: California prosecutors, victim advocates challenge Newsom's mass death sentence commutation
keyFacts: California prosecutors and victims' advocates are challenging Gov. Gavin Newsom's commutation of 548 death sentences to life without parole.
Modoc County District Attorney Nina Salarno and other critics stated that the blanket action denied victims' families a voice in the clemency process.
A coalition of district attorneys and law enforcement groups filed a petition with the California Supreme Court to halt the commutations.
body: California Gov. Gavin Newsom justified his blanket commutation of 548 death sentences to life without parole by arguing that reviewing cases individually would create "two classes of murder victims," a rationale victims' advocates and at least one district attorney called "morally offensive. "
Modoc County District Attorney Nina Salarno said Newsom's sweeping action denied the loved ones of murder victims any voice in the clemency process.

"I found it really offensive as a victim myself, and [for] my other victims," Salarno told Fox News Digital from Washington, D. C., where she and fellow advocates met with President Donald Trump this week. "There should be individual scrutiny. The individual victims should have a voice. And that's what he has avoided by doing a blanket commutation."
CALIFORNIA PROSECUTORS SLAM NEWSOM'S DEATH ROW COMMUTATIONS, ACCUSE GOVERNOR OF PUTTING 'POLITICS OVER PEOPLE'
"The blanket commutation on a moral level as a victim I find very offensive, but I find the whole thing offensive to our entire rule of law," she added.

Topo Padilla, president of Crime Victims United, a nonprofit that advocates for stricter laws against violent offenders, noted that California voters have repeatedly upheld the death penalty at the ballot box, including approving a 2016 measure aimed at speeding up executions.

"Here's a guy who throws rocks about kings and protests throughout the streets," Padilla said, referring to Newsom's past criticisms of Trump. "I will promise you, this is a move that is looked at and viewed as a king. He is trampling on the voters."

On Monday, Trump vowed to direct the Justice Department to seek the death penalty for child murderers and expedite federal executions as victims’ relatives spoke out at the Justice Department against Newsom's order.
SLAIN FIREFIGHTER'S MOTHER PLEADS WITH TRUMP TO INTERVENE AFTER NEWSOM STOPS KILLER'S DEATH SENTENCE

"Gavin Newsom and the radical left look at these heinous acts, and their sympathy is not for the children and their parents, but for the monsters who extinguished innocent young lives," Trump said. "He stood with the murderers and child slayers."
Justice for crime victims shouldn't be a partisan issue, Padilla said.
"Whether you're a Democrat or a Republican, you take politics out of this," he said. "The president of the United States stood up and sounded the alarm. And I hope the country hears it."
Newsom's office referred Fox News Digital to news release from Monday featuring victims and survivors who support his decision.
GAVIN NEWSOM WIPES OUT CALIFORNIA'S DEATH ROW IN HISTORIC MASS COMMUTATION

"As a member of the clergy, I believe that all life is sacred. I also believe in the possibility of redemption. Because of this, I oppose the death penalty," said Rabbi Suzanne Singer, the sister of Michele Reiner and sister-in-law of famed film director Rob Reiner, who were both stabbed to death in December 2025 inside their Los Angeles home.

"As a civilized nation, it is barbaric that we still subject people to die at the hands of the state. I am so grateful to Governor Newsom for commuting the death sentences that have been imposed in our state. This is true proof of his moral character."

On Nov. 16, a coalition of roughly 30 county district attorneys, law enforcement groups, victims' rights advocates and grieving families filed a petition with the California Supreme Court seeking to halt Newsom's commutations .
MICHAEL RUIZ: DA IDENTIFIES 49 LOCAL KILLERS SLATED FOR NEWSOM'S DEATH ROW CLEMENCY — AND THEIR CRIMES

Salarno argued that the governor's move disrespects the jurors and judges who endured months-long capital trials . Even though California has not carried out an execution since 2006, Padilla noted that the death sentence itself provides essential legal validation and finality for grieving families, a loss he knows firsthand.

"The fact of the matter is the law is the law," Padilla said. "It's like changing the innings in a baseball game, changing from nine to seven retroactively, going back [and] going, 'I know you won that game, but we're going to make it seven innings and now you lost.'"
CALIFORNIA DA SAYS GAVIN NEWSOM'S 'CRUEL' DEATH ROW CLEMENCY STABS CRIME VICTIMS 'IN THE HEART'

The fight is also deeply personal for Salarno, whose older sister, Catina Rose Salarno, was murdered in 1979 on her first day at the University of the Pacific by her former high school boyfriend, Steven Burns. Following the tragedy, Salarno's mother, Harriet, founded Crime Victims United.

"Look, my sister's never coming back, and I understand that," Padilla added. "But I have to accept that she was murdered, like these families have to accept that their loved ones were. And we have to trust the justice system. And now it's been taken away from them. And that's where I think the real issue comes."

articles.headline: Dell and HPE both say they’ve become ‘different companies’
keyFacts: Dell and HPE both told investors on their respective earnings calls this week that they have become different companies.
HPE CEO Antonio Neri attributed the change to acquiring Juniper Networks and building products for artificial intelligence.
Dell COO Jeff Clarke said the Infrastructure Solutions Group now provides the vast majority of the company profit and growth.
body: Dell and HPE this week both told investors they’ve become “different companies.”

The two hardware giants made that assertion on their respective earnings calls this week. HPE went first, on Monday, when CEO Antonio Neri declared “We are now a fundamentally different company” after acquiring Juniper Networks and creating products “built to capitalize on the next phase of AI.”

On Tuesday, Dell’s chief operating officer and vice chairman Jeff Clarke declared “We are now a different company” because the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) has become the source of “the vast majority of our profit and growth.”
HPE’s claim to having changed is perhaps more credible on the face of it, given that its acquisition of Juniper means it has become more of a networking player.

Dell hasn’t made significant additions to its hardware portfolio, but there’s a big difference in its sources of revenue, which three years ago was just about evenly split between its infrastructure and client devices. In its Tuesday announcement, Dell revealed ISG revenue grew 198 percent year over year to $42 billion, while CSG racked up three percent growth to $12.9 billion – meaning Dell is now predominantly an infrastructure company.
Clarke said he’s seen some companies deferring their PC purchases to buy AI hardware instead, and said Dell is re-assigning parts it ordered to build PCs and using them for servers instead.

Dell exited its Q3 with a backlog of $32 billion worth of AI servers and is clearly aware that investors might worry that’s not a useful metric because some buyers’ dreams of operating neoclouds have struck financial or regulatory barriers. Clarke assured investors that Dell is “highly selective about the partners we work with”
“Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance, and access to land and power.”

HPE also has wrinkles in its AI business, because buyers won’t stand for fat margins and that’s dented the company’s profits a little. Neri was able to point to AI-related revenue also rising sharply, up 68.6 percent year over year to $11.3 billion, while overall revenue climbed 50 percent to reach $14.5 billion. Networking grew at a more relaxed 12 percent.

The CEO said HPE expects better growth ahead, because new server purchases create demand for networks and storage. He also pointed to HPE having the opportunity to sell its networking kit to other OEMs who build AMD’s Helios rack-scale systems. HPE predicted its next quarter will see revenue reach $14.0 billion to $14.6 billion, up 51 to 57 percent year over year.

Dell is also optimistic that AI buyers will spend on kit beyond servers and GPUs and updated its full-year revenue outlook to $202 billion, $10 billion above its previous forecasts and up 78 percent year over year. ®
