articles.headline: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
keyFacts: FinCEN disclosed on Tuesday that it is investigating a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.
FinCEN stated that it has taken some systems offline as a precaution while the scope and source of the breach remain unverified.
FinCEN reported that banks can still file suspicious activity reports online and use an unaffected hotline for expedited reports.
body: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed on Tuesday that it’s investigating a “cybersecurity incident.” The bureau, which is part of the Treasury Department, said it’s looking into an “incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.” It hasn’t offered any information about the full scope or source of the breach, but FinCEN has taken some systems offline as a precaution.
US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
FinCEN’s alert comes in the wake of a reported breach of unclassified information at US spy agencies, including the CIA.

The news comes hours after The New York Times reported that the Central Intelligence Agency and Office of the Director of National Security discovered a breach of an open source intelligence system, exposing unclassified information. The Department of Defense, whose National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency was also reportedly impacted by the breach, declined to comment. The CIA and ODNI did not immediately respond to requests for comment. It’s unclear if the FinCEN breach is related. Americans have been on high alert about security incidents after a series of seemingly unrelated outages earlier this month.
Americans have been on high alert about security incidents

FinCEN’s role is to protect the financial system from illegal activity, including by combatting money laundering and terrorism financing. The bureau maintains financial transaction data and distributes it for law enforcement purposes. FinCEN also houses reports of suspicious activity that financial institutions file as part of the Bank Secrecy Act.

FinCEN says in its alert that banks can still file reports about suspicious activity online, but some services may not be immediately available. Filers that need to expedite their reports in the meantime can still call the Financial Institutions Hotline, which it says was not impacted by the disruption.
Update, November 24th: Added response from Department of Defense.

articles.headline: Change this Roku TV setting to watch movies how they were filmed
keyFacts: Engadget reported that Roku TVs can have their default 60fps refresh rate changed to match the 24fps rate used for movies.
Users can enable this feature by navigating through the Settings, System, Advanced System Settings, and Advanced Display Settings menus on their Roku TV.
Engadget stated that turning on the auto-adjust display refresh rate setting allows the TV to automatically match the native frame rate of movies or shows.
body: Change this Roku TV setting to watch movies how they were filmed
You don't have to leave your TV's refresh rate at 60fps.

If you were to travel back in time thirty years and show someone a smart TV from today, their head would likely explode. In addition to the seemingly limitless amount of content one can find and interact with on a modern television, your Roku TV also may have the ability to let you watch movies in a far more compelling way.

Buried deep in your Roku TV's settings is a way to alter the refresh rate, and there's a very specific reason that you might want to do that. Most Roku TVs default to a refresh rate of 60fps. While that's going to be perfectly fine for some situations, it doesn't make for the most theatrical viewing experience — for the most part, movies are filmed and projected at 24fps. It's the standard, and it has defined the way movies look and feel for decades. When you go to the movie theater, you're watching a 24fps output.
Roku allows you to alter your TV's refresh rate to match that, offering something a bit closer to the original intent of those films.
How to change your TV's refresh rate to 24fps to achieve a film look

There are a lot of ways to change the overall look and display of your Roku TV, but most of that discourse seems centered around colors and contrast. Those things are important, but if you really want to achieve a "movie look," then you'll want to change the refresh rate.

In your Roku TV, to match this unique look, you'll need to first go to the main menu. From here, select Settings, and then go into System. In this menu, you'll find something called Advanced System Settings, which will allow you to access Advanced Display Settings. You want to turn Auto-adjust display refresh rate on.

It's a one-click and done solution, as it will self-adjust itself to match the native refresh rate of any movie or TV show you put on. Because films have a native refresh rate of 24fps, your TV will now run them as such. The same goes for TV shows, which may be filmed at 30 or 60fps. It's a tiny adjustment, but it's one that will make your viewing experience even better.

articles.headline: The Actor Behind GTA 6′s Viral NPC Mandy Reacts To All Of The Attention: ‘It’s Sort Of Bittersweet’
keyFacts: Actor Lexie Shoaibi said the viral internet fame surrounding her role as Mandy in Grand Theft Auto 6 is bittersweet.
Shoaibi stated she auditioned for the role in 2023 without knowing it was for Grand Theft Auto 6 and later discovered her appearance through online streaming clips.
Shoaibi reported that online impersonators have emerged following her sudden fame, prompting her to warn followers about fake accounts.
body: Mandy is one of the first NPCs players run into in Grand Theft Auto 6. Jason is sent to collect rent from her and she tries to come onto him despite his Mr. Freeze levels of cold disinterest. At one point he’s trying to unscrew the bolt for the sink trap when she comes back wearing nothing but a pink-trimmed leopard-print string bikini. Clips of the early encounter quickly went viral. Actor Lexie Shoaibi, who voices Mandy, said the instant internet fame has been “bittersweet.”

Like many video game characters, Mandy is modeled after one person but voiced by another. The model is Miami-based influencer Marissa DuBois. The voice belongs to Shoaibi, an actor and model who also promotes herself through Meta’s engagement-driven algorithm. She told Vulture that she auditioned for the role back around 2023, but it was never explicitly confirmed to her that it was for GTA 6.

The context-less gig came with tons of NDAs, but Shoaibi found the performance part surprisingly inviting. She performed opposite Jason’s actor, Dylan Rourke, and said the whole experience felt a bit like an “off-Broadway theater production.” It wasn’t until years later, when she saw clips of streamers playing the game on November 18, that she realized what she’d appeared in and got to see the finished performance. Within 24 hours, Mandy was a thirst trap on every GTA subreddit.

“I think because I have some experience with online attention as a content creator, Iâve developed a pretty effective lens for seeing more good than bad,” Shoaibi said when asked about having the Gooner Eye of Sauron laser in on her. “There are weirdos out there, and theyâre going to try to bring you down, so itâs important to stay around the people and the places that arenât doing that. Itâs easy enough to do, which Iâm very grateful for. Thereâs enough support in my real-life community and online that I can say, ‘I could just hang out over here. I donât actually need to go to the scary place.’ Iâm living in the positive, for sure.”

The actor recently appeared on a Twitch charity stream with Hasan Piker, who she was put in contact with by a mutual friend. The 15 minutes of video game fame has led to a bunch of people impersonating her online as people try to chase clout in Mandy’s wake. âI donât know how that happened,â Shoaibi told Piker (via IGN). âPeople pretending to be me? Itâs thrilling. Please stop, but itâs also so exciting. Itâs sort of bittersweet.â She had previously put out a warning on her Instagram about fake accounts trying to pose as her.

The most surprising moment during Jason’s initial encounter with Mandy is when he discovers the cause of the clogged sink: a human finger. She takes it from him so fast that you can easily miss what it actually is, but clues scattered around the rest of her house reveal she might be something of a serial killer. Shoaibi said she had no idea about that part of the character ahead of time.

“When we were recording, it wasnât specifically clarified or intended for me to base my acting around,” she told Vulture. “On the motion-capture set, it was just a little colorful block. I think we played with ‘finger,’ but it might also at one point have been ‘a toe’–not that thatâs so different. But I wasnât led to believe it was an important clue to who she is and what sheâs up to. It was just some weirdness in the sink. Thatâs what I got.”

articles.headline: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
keyFacts: Yale academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld stated that Nvidia is a detriment to U.S. industrial might because its advanced chips have reached China despite export controls.
President Trump and administration officials pressured Nvidia's board to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang following heavy lobbying and private weekend calls.
Nvidia and its directors face multiple shareholder lawsuits, federal investigations, and congressional inquiries regarding leadership actions and chip security.
body: Investors cheered Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday, but renowned business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale thinks they’re celebrating a mistake. He sees a company that is largely responsible for putting sophisticated technology in the hands of the country’s adversaries, at a moment when the risks couldn’t be higher. Far from a champion of American industry, he says, Nvidia is “a detriment to U.S. global industrial might.”

As evidence, Sonnenfeld points to research suggesting Nvidia’s most advanced chips have reached China despite U.S. export controls and to sinking shares of Anthropic, which he links to the realization that China’s seemingly miraculous open source AI models are, in a sense, copies of top U.S. labs’ work, even as Nvidia has insisted that smuggling is a “non-factor.”
Indeed, Huang’s return was greeted with just as much enthusiasm in Asia, The Washington Post reported. “The king is back!” read one headline from China’s state-affiliated Star Market Daily.

The reinstatement itself followed heavy pressure from Washington. Nvidia’s chairman had effectively ruled out Huang’s return just last week. Then, in a torrent of private weekend calls led by Vice President JD Vance, top administration officials leaned on the board to welcome Huang back, with President Trump calling the board directly to vouch for him. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC on Monday.

Sonnenfeld says the directors who went along, and who returned Huang to the board even as it investigates whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted him, now face a “historic level of individual liability.”

The legal deluge has already begun. As we noted a couple of weeks ago, a potential class-action lawsuit was filed almost immediately. Days later, a shareholder derivative suit followed. Filed on Nvidia’s behalf against the directors themselves, the suit alleges the board ignored red flags about Huang’s relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang.

The class action is very much aimed at making Nvidia and Huang compensate investors for their losses, while the derivative suit puts the directors’ own behavior on trial, with any recovery going to Nvidia. Three more suits followed on November 18, the day after Nvidia’s most recent earnings call; all five were filed in Northern California, where Nvidia is based.

Huang and Nvidia are also juggling a Justice Department antitrust investigation, a reported SEC probe into Nvidia’s accounting, a possible FBI review, a California subpoena, an export-control case that landed partner Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist on Monday, and congressional inquiries, including a Senate Banking hearing next week at which Huang has agreed to testify.
Here’s more of what Sonnenfeld had to say, in a Q&A that’s been edited for length and clarity.
So much has happened since we last talked. Huang was ousted, he’s come back. Do you think the board’s reliance on government assurances here is defensible or an abdication of its own duties?

They failed to rely on experts. That’s one of the reasons this board is going to be sued and lose, and these directors are likely to face a historic level of individual liability. They have a very inadequate directors and officers liability policy. They have also just failed in their diligence. They hired the Wachtell [law] firm. The Wachtell firm barely got off the blocks to do an investigation. And then they have already reversed themselves, so they didn’t use the expertise needed.
It’s wild that they also put Huang right back on the board of directors.

The board showed, in addition to incompetence and collaboration, just cowardice in their capitulation because Trump has nothing to wave over them. If this was SpaceX, where 46% of its business comes from the government [you could maybe see the case for Trump’s involvement]. For Nvidia, it’s not even 1% of its business that comes from the U.S. government, so [the board] didn’t have that threat. [Trump] can call off [federal] investigations, but he can’t call off the shareholder litigation. Some are already filed, and the estimates are there’ll probably be 30 of them, and they’re going to be extremely costly.

And this is not, by the way, just a blue or red state issue. We already have 14 GOP senators who’ve already come out against this, and very prominent conservatives, like Pete Ricketts and Josh Hawley and Tom Cotton and John Cornyn. Those are some issues that may help explain why Nvidia’s stock is tumbling today.
Might the board say, “We saw the classified intelligence findings, and they assure us Jensen will be absolved of wrongdoing”?

They haven’t seen those findings, and we also haven’t seen what will be the result of the Senate Intelligence Committee, the Senate Special Committee on Investigations, the Senate Banking Committee, and all their House counterparts. The board hasn’t seen any of that, and even if they saw it, which they have not yet, that still wouldn’t matter.
Do you think the Commerce Department will continue to tighten its chip export controls to keep China from accessing so much compute or walk back some of those recent moves?

We already see that Megaspeed has finally been put on the sanctions list, as it should have been before. And we have documentation now that Nvidia, rather than a champion of U.S. global industrial might, is actually a detriment to U.S. global industrial might, because their chips have now turned out to be in the hands and in the systems of not just the Chinese military, as they got channeled to Northwestern Polytechnical University, which is a military institution — this is going into weapons that will, of course, be funneled to Iran and Russia, and they didn’t have access to that a year ago. [Editor’s note: China has long denied supplying weapons to either country. Nvidia chips have been found in Russian drones, however, and the U.S. ambassador to China said in September that President Trump had discussed selling arms to China, an account Trump has denied.]

The open source models that people have celebrated and marveled at — that China somehow has this ingenuity to be creating their own chips, so that Kimi and DeepSeek and these other celebrated open source models were producing a miracle of Anthropic-like results — turns out we know why. They are pirating it. They are “distilling it” from Anthropic using high-end Nvidia chips.
Nvidia has denied reports that its most advanced chips have been smuggled into China.

There’s an Israeli company, Lava, that just three weeks ago showed [dozens of] Blackwell chips are in China. We’re seeing, with the return of Jensen Huang, Anthropic plummet. Why would that be? Of course, this is because it’s hurting OpenAI. It’s hurting Grok. It’s hurting Perplexity. It’s hurting Gemini. And you’ve seen none of these tech titans celebrate this. We have the misogynist tech bros holding locker-room-type rallies about Jensen Huang’s return, but nobody else has spoken out in favor of this. [You’re not hearing from] the CEOs of Microsoft or IBM or J.P. Morgan or Walmart or General Motors or Caterpillar. Nobody thinks that this is a good move.
You don’t think Nvidia needed Huang back?

He was not the guy designing the chips. It’s important to point out that that’s a guy named Chris Malachowsky, a co-founder who’s still there who designed these GPUs and has a whole team of next-generation people like Jonah Alben doing the chip design. As for the great software that has leveraged these chips, that’s also not Jensen Huang. That’s a guy named Ian Buck, who’s been very much celebrated in the last two weeks. He’s the one who designed the CUDA software that leverages the chips. Those people weren’t going anywhere, and wherever Jensen Huang is has nothing to do with them.
Some are trying to make Huang’s forced resignation about the extramarital affairs to which he has admitted, calling it HR policy gone wild.
A CEO who doesn’t stand by his own code of conduct makes it completely unenforceable.
Wired quoted an Nvidia employee who said they’d never take an HR training course again if Huang was reinstated.

This thing is a sexual affair with a subordinate — whether it’s coercion, or even if it truly was somehow consensual, it’s not fair. Every decision on resource allocation, on staffing, on product decisions, is not objective. It’s either favoritism, or, if the relationship fails, retribution. All the other people on that team rise and fall with a sexual relationship; it’s something they have no control over.

articles.headline: Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia takes founder worship to a dangerous level
keyFacts: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returned to lead the trillion-dollar company after President Donald Trump pressured the board to reinstate him.
Huang remains under investigation regarding his relationship with a tech executive tied to a Chinese spy agency and illegal chip smuggling.
Experts warned that failing to hold the leader of the AI industry accountable creates unprecedented risks for the American economy.
body: President Donald Trump greets Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang outside the West Wing following a meeting about AI on September 29, 2026. | Getty Images

The news of Jensen Huang’s resurrection at Nvidia felt like a practical joke or an Onion headline. Here was a cofounder and CEO of a trillion-dollar company who did just about all the bad things a CEO could do — including maybe involvement in espionage — who’d gotten his comeuppance. The board did its job. The investigations commenced, and Huang resigned in a rare moment of accountability in Silicon Valley culture.

But that’s not how the story ended. Huang quickly returned to the helm of Nvidia thanks to his personal friend, the president of the United States, Donald Trump, who had pressured the board to reinstate the disgraced founder. (“I made the deal,” Trump told a television audience.) When the newly vindicated CEO walked back into Nvidia headquarters on Monday, ecstatic employees cheered his name — “Jensen! Jensen!”

Considering the larger context, this is absurd. Huang is still under investigation at Nvidia, the company that he’s once again running, over his relationship with a tech executive, Alice Huang, who’d been talking to China’s top spy agency during the affair. And she’s under investigation over her alleged role in smuggling illegal Nvidia chips into China.

“It’s the worst degradation in corporate governance in American history and the greatest business-government scandal in US history,” Jeffrey Sonnenfeld , the senior associate dean for leadership studies at Yale School of Management, told me a couple of hours after the news broke. “I mean, this is crazy.”
Key takeaways
Silicon Valley’s founder worship started with a bad founder. In the 1950s, eight employees could no longer work for their mercurial visionary founder, so they became visionary founders themselves.
Huang’s comeback shows how tech company boards still can’t control their founders. President Trump pushed Nvidia’s board to reinstate him while the company was still investigating him.
Nvidia supplies the chips behind the AI boom and finances the companies buying them. When so much rides on one company, failing to hold its founder accountable can put the entire economy at risk.

This is not just a matter of poor corporate governance; it is a profound collision of two visions for the future: First, there’s the founder-worshipping tradition of Silicon Valley, where visionaries not only can but should get away with anything in the name of profit and progress. Then there are the people and institutions, like the media and the government, who hold power to account and make sure this big beautiful American experiment doesn’t unravel completely.

It’s not unusual for these two groups to clash. But the stakes today are higher than they’ve been in a long time. Nvidia is not only the primary supplier of chips and software to the AI boom, it’s also the industry’s chief financier, funding startups that will buy those chips and infrastructure that makes everything work. If Nvidia faltered, the whole house of cards could come down, bringing the American economy down with it . Many of the founder-worshipping class considered Huang irreplaceable , which would mean the future of the nation depended on his employment status.

Jensen Huang’s restoration to his seat of power shows that Silicon Valley’s vision for the future may be winning out: The wealthiest individuals in our society operate with no baseline accountability. And even when they make colossal mistakes, their friend, the president, can restore their power.
It wasn’t supposed to be like this, but in a sense, we’ve been heading this direction for a long time.
Founder worship is as old as electricity

The cult of the founder lives on X these days. That’s where you could find tech leaders and venture capital types calling for Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia and then cheering the news when it happened. Their specific arguments or grievances about Huang being pushed out seem both ridiculous and familiar (investor and podcaster Jason Calacanis seems to think that journalism is the villain here). But beneath the rhetoric is a philosophy about the importance of an all-knowing and all-powerful tech founder that’s as old as computers and electricity itself.

The tradition of worshipping the infallible founder dates back to Thomas Edison, and it’s always been central to the American tech industry, which values visionary thinking and nimble leadership above all else. You can trace the roots of this culture back to the 1950s, when a startup called Fairchild Semiconductor laid the foundation of Silicon Valley as we know it today. Fairchild made some of the first microchips, which would have made it legendary in its own right. But there was a cultural component to how the company was founded, how it was run, and what its alums went on to do that has shaped tech culture ever since.

Fairchild was actually a spinoff of another chip company, Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory, founded by the co-inventor of the transistor, William Shockley. You could argue that Shockley was the original visionary founder-CEO in Silicon Valley, down to his problematic management style, which drove employees to start their own firm in 1957. Known as the “Traitorous Eight,” a group of them — including Robert Noyce, founder of Intel, and Gordon Moore, the Moore in Moore’s Law — left Shockley to start the new company. Fairchild Semiconductor got its funding and name from Fairchild Camera and Instrument, an East Coast company that thrived on military contracts for its spy satellite equipment. They eschewed the idea of letting a founder-visionary dictate its business in favor of a flat organizational structure.

The pursuit of wealth is actually where you’ll find some of Nvidia’s ancestral roots. After leaving Fairchild Semiconductor, Eugene Kleiner and Don Valentine became the pioneers of modern venture capital, starting Kleiner Perkins and Sequoia Capital, respectively in 1972. Valentine went on to fund early Silicon Valley success stories — Atari, Apple, Cisco, and Oracle, to name a few — and revered the so-called brilliant entrepreneur. According to the venture capitalist Fred Wilson, Valentine once said , “Sometimes we make money with brilliant people who are easy to get along with, most often we make money with brilliant people who are hard to get along with, but we rarely make money with normal people who are easy to get along with.”

It was during Valentine’s era that we saw the cult of the founder start to form around people like Steve Jobs or Larry Ellison. Then, Sequoia Partners became the first major investor in a little chip company called Nvidia. He was actually in the room when Jensen Huang gave the original pitch in 1993. Huang apparently bombed the pitch, but Valentine invested in the venture based on the Nvidia cofounder’s reputation. The way Huang tells it , when Valentine shook his hand, he looked him square in the eye and said, “If you lose my money, I will kill you.”
At market close Monday, the day Huang was reinstated, Nvidia was worth nearly $4 trillion.
“The misfits, the rebels, the troublemakers.”

The founders still worshipped in Silicon Valley have always been hailed as outsiders and disruptors. Look no further than the commercial Steve Jobs narrated not long after his triumphant return to Apple about “the misfits, the rebels, the troublemakers.” It ends: “The ones who are crazy enough to think that they can change the world, are the ones who do.”

There’s something very American about this idea of taking risks and changing the world — it’s also a great way to get rich. Noyce and Moore went on to become some of the wealthiest businessmen in the country. Huang’s net worth surged by $36 billion the day he returned as Nvidia’s CEO.

Tech founders’ success has also always come with baggage. Icons like Jobs and Ellison changed the world — but also had reputations as bad bosses . Jobs was known for publicly humiliating his employees, for being spiteful and controlling . He took credit for his employees’ work, and his biographer, Walter Isaacson, has called him “the world’s worst manager.” Apparently, everyone who worked for Ellison hated him . Both men started out as outsiders, but then they became billionaires running some of the biggest companies in the world. Their abusive management styles then became something of a hallmark, proof of their durable genius.

Corporate boards exist to rein in this kind of behavior. But in reality, they often do no such thing when it comes to dealing with visionary founders. The board of OpenAI fired Sam Altman as CEO three years ago over an alleged lack of transparency — or simply lying to them, if you want a shorthand. But following a loud campaign by his supporters in Silicon Valley, not unlike the campaign to reinstate Huang, Altman was back to work less than a week later , and the company replaced its entire board.

Then there’s Elon Musk, who had to resign as Tesla’s chair to settle fraud charges in 2018, although he kept his role as CEO. Although he’s faced calls to step down as chair, Mark Zuckerberg has been CEO of Meta since he started the company in his Harvard dorm room, despite losing $77 billion on his failed metaverse bet. WeWork’s Adam Neumann, Theranos’s Elizabeth Holmes, and Uber’s Travis Kalanick were all founder-CEOs who lost their jobs due to bad behavior — intense risk taking , defrauding investors , and just lots of scandals , respectively. Those three stand apart because their boards did not invite them to come back.

Huang, for what it’s worth, had been a pretty boring founder-CEO up until recently. Well before the free money era, Nvidia got its start making graphics processing units (GPUs) which were primarily used in video game systems. Huang eventually steered the company in more ambitious directions, leveraging the company’s technology to become central to the burgeoning AI industry.

It wasn’t until the release of ChatGPT in 2022 kicked off the AI boom that Huang became a household name. In the years that followed, as demand for Nvidia chips skyrocketed and zeroes started multiplying on the ends of its revenue numbers, we got to know him as a showman, a storyteller, and a lover of black leather jackets . He had become a tech titan and, according to one magazine cover , “The Sorcerer of Silicon.”

Over the years, Huang had also developed a reputation as an abusive manager who humiliated employees in front of their peers. He reportedly told one that he’d rip off their arms and beat them over the head with them. He hired his family members as subordinate executives. Huang became the epitome of the visionary founder, personality flaws and all.

What really sets Huang apart from his visionary founder predecessors is the scale of what Nvidia’s become — and what he’s come to represent. Huang has made himself indispensable at Nvidia in a number of ways, guarding his role as the company’s primary dealmaker, and ensuring through his 60 direct reports that succession would be complicated. And because Nvidia plays such a central role in the AI boom, as the main supplier of advanced chips needed to train and run the most powerful models, Huang made himself the main character of the entire AI industry, much like Trump made himself the singular figure in Republican politics.

Margaret O’Mara , an American history professor at the University of Washington, called Huang’s reinstatement “remarkable even by Silicon Valley’s founder-centric standards.” There have been plenty of examples of tech founders who lost their companies but held onto the support of their cult-like following. Some people even think Elizabeth Holmes still deserves another chance . But the scale of what Huang is responsible for and the scale of what he’s accused of doing have reached new heights.

“America has never experienced such extreme concentration of wealth and market value in such a small number of leaders and companies, and I don’t think this move will do much to slow Americans’ growing unease with the AI boom and its biggest boosters,” O’Mara said.

The US economy finds itself at a choke point that’s not dissimilar to where Nvidia found itself when Huang resigned, surrounded by scandals. The company had been organized around a single visionary who had led them to unprecedented success but, upon his fall, could represent an existential threat.

It actually seemed like it could be good news for Nvidia to rethink its leadership structure in the wake of Huang’s scandals; perhaps even the AI industry would find more stability when it didn’t depend so much on one company’s brilliant entrepreneur to call the shots. Plus, companies do better when they take their leaders’ misbehavior seriously.

The most dangerous part about this moment is not only that we’re back where we started. It’s also that we can see where we could have corrected our course — the exact moment where we could have held a visionary founder accountable for his reckless behavior — but didn’t.

articles.headline: GTA 6's Most Heartbreaking Scene Is Exactly Why You Had To Do All Those Chores
keyFacts: Grand Theft Auto 6 features mundane early-game chores where Jason repairs and prepares a home for Lucia's return from prison.
Jason and Lucia accept a risky job from Mattia to deliver a mysterious bag, resulting in a shootout and their arrest.
Masked criminals attack Jason and Lucia's home, destroying the house and the personal memories inside it in a tragic fire.
body: Grand Theft Auto 6 features as much shootin’, stealin’, and drug runnin’ as you’d expect from the latest entry in a series named after a felony. However, some players have been caught off-guard by just how much the early game is all about the more mundane parts of life. Namely, you gotta do a bunch of chores around the house. In many ways, GTA 6 is as much of an everyday life sim as it is a game about committing crimes.

Jason repairs the steps leading up to his and Lucia’s home, fixes a railing, buys groceries, orders flowers, paints the walls of their bedroom, and more to prepare for Lucia’s arrival from prison. All those chores might seem less thrilling than the opening hours you’d expect in a big-budget action game. But it turns out they set up a tragic heartbreak I simply did not see coming.
[Ed. note: Spoilers for the ending of Chapter 1 follow.]

Chapter 1 involves Jason and Lucia trying to get work from Mattia, the shady boyfriend of Kat, a mother-to-be whom Lucia befriended in prison. Part of that involves a standout sequence set to a Carly Rae Jepsen banger before Lucia gets lost in orgy central. (Vice City, y’all!) Bro, Mattia promises a job that could pay ten grand, bro. They just have to grab a bag from a locker and deliver it, bro.

Red flags abound, but Jason and Lucia go along for the ride, which quickly results in their arrest. Crooked cops show up, the couple gets into a shootout, and Jason gets grievously wounded while the couple struggle to keep hold over a bag containing who knows what.

GTA 6 does a great job of showing how various systems, both governmental and societal, are against Jason and Lucia, and that shines through here. In Jason and Lucia, Mattia sees a pair of not prospective partners, but a down-on-their-luck couple he can easily exploit — and they’re all too willing to play into his hands. Mattia leverages their desperation, even making them play dress up with Lucia in a platinum blonde wig and Jason in one of Mattia’s gaudy shirts, so they’d take the fall for whatever shady shit Mattia is up to. Clearly, he knew the danger surrounding this bag with shady cops and an organized outfit after it and gladly fed Jason and Lucia to the wolves.

They escape, but their horrible night has only just begun. Lucia takes Jason to his friend Cal, who brings Jason — and the mysterious bag — to the hospital. (Lucia later learns the hospital took everything from the couple’s BuckMe checking account as payment. America!) Lucia heads home to recover Jason’s stash, and tragedy strikes.

Upon entering their home, Lucia is jumped by masked criminals searching for that bag. Suddenly, the home Jason and Lucia built is now the arena for Lucia’s fight for her life. Flames engulf the sliding glass door that led to a patio where Jason would work out and the couple would hold one another while sipping their coffee and enjoying the morning sun. Those relaxing mornings are no more.

Tommy’s future crib that Jason bought during his video game night with Cal? Destroyed. A goon even tosses Lucia into it at one point, adding insult to injury. Where Tommy would have slept soundlessly — with a giant stuffed teddy in the corner — is now burning up. Also burning up is the hope that Jason and Lucia will get to live a normal life with Tommy, which the crib represented. Maybe in another life Jason and Lucia would have told Mattia to eat shit, bro, stayed patient, and welcomed Tommy to their little house on stilts in due time. Not in this life, however.

Watching the coffee table get destroyed hurt even more. Building furniture together with a shaky hex key is a quintessential couples activity, and Jason and Lucia do just that during a cute sequence earlier in the game. And then one of the masked men slams Lucia on it, shattering its glass top as their home continues to burn.

Flames raged after I dispatched those enemies. Still, I tried to have Lucia grab the stash from their burning bedroom, only to see her immediately get burned. (She’s fine.) I didn’t want the stash for the money, but the memories.

In Jason’s metal box, he has polaroid pictures showing him as a baby in his mother’s arms, him in football pads with his best friends, him with Lucia, and him with his army buddies. Jason’s a pretty stoic guy, so I wouldn’t expect him to outright say what these artifacts mean to him, but him keeping them alongside his rainy day fund says all it needs to. But, just like the crib, coffee table, and everything else, they’re gone. At least I was able to save the photo of Tommy, but not before screaming at my TV thinking I had missed it.

The house going up in flames is tragic on so many levels. It represented stability for the pair, a stability that they no longer have while trying to survive out of a crappy motel in Chapter 2’s Port Gellhorn. Not only did Jason spend his time fixing it up, but I spent my time fixing it up. I was immediately invested in that home as a result of the work I put into it. Now, it’s a pile of ash.

Everyone whining about the beginning segment of GTA 6 (how dare a game starring a romantic couple have an optional mission for the boyfriend to buy his girlfriend a necklace) missed the forest for the trees. Not only are the activities building a relationship between Jason and Lucia, but between the player and their controllable avatars. I’m over 20% into the story now, and I’ve already come to care for these two knuckleheads in the same way I care for characters in a BioWare game or my Baldur’s Gate 3 companions.

Rockstar’s GTA 6 has taken me by surprise every step of the way with how strong its writing is. I was a bit trepidatious going into it. Could any one game live up to years of massive hype, especially the highest-rated game ever? With its spotlight on two complex lead characters just trying to make it another day in a messed-up world, it’s delivered in spades. At the very least, no other game has made me care about a goddamn coffee table like GTA 6 has.

articles.headline: Bellingham plays down Zidane comparison after wonder goal
keyFacts: Manager Jose Mourinho called Jude Bellingham the best midfielder in the world after Bellingham scored a wonder goal in Real Madrid's 5-1 win against PSV.
Bellingham dismissed comparisons to Zinedine Zidane, stating that Zidane is much better and is his idol.
Bellingham stated that he does not care about individual awards like the Ballon d'Or and is only focused on winning team titles.
body: - Published

Manager Jose Mourinho described Jude Bellingham as "without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world" following a wonder goal which inspired a brilliant second-half performance for Real Madrid in a 5-1 win against PSV.

Mourinho opted to leave the England midfielder out of the starting line-up for Tuesday's Champions League game at the Bernabeu - an understandable decision given the demands of Madrid's fixture schedule and the strength in depth at his disposal.
But after watching his side trail 1-0 at half-time against the Dutch side, Mourinho knew changes were needed.
On came Bellingham.

"He is an amazing player that has everything," the Portuguese manager said. "He has physicality, he understands the game, he has absolutely everything. Today, he has changed how the game was evolving."
Captain Fede Valverde equalised in the 50th minute and 10 minutes later Bellingham produced his moment of magic.

Receiving the ball just outside the penalty area, he took two touches to lift it into position before unleashing a magnificent volley with the outside of his right footr, leaving PSV keeper Matej Kovar with no chance.
It was a sensational finish, executed with extraordinary precision.

"I was a bit surprised, honestly," Bellingham said about the goal. "I knew that I could control the ball well and get it into my grasp. But normally from there, I'm looking to see who's on as an option to play through.
"It popped up nicely and I thought I'm just going to hit it. So yeah, it was a nice goal and important for the team, being the second goal, and gave us control."
The 23-year-old celebrated in trademark fashion, standing with his arms outstretched in front of the home supporters as thousands serenaded him with chants of 'Hey Jude'.
It was his fourth goal in his past five appearances for Real.
Asked whether he should be compared to Real and France legend Zinedine Zidane, who won the Ballon d'Or and World Cup in 1998, Bellingham maintained his humility.
"I think Zidane is much better than me. He's much more elegant and he's my idol," he said.
'I don't care about the Ballon d'Or'
Kylian Mbappe scored two more goals and Vinicius Junior put away the fifth to complete a super turnaround from a team that had looked short of ideas in the first half.
At the suggestion that he is currently in the form of his life, Bellingham said: "I think you're only as good as your next one [game]. Your last one doesn't really matter.
"But my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game. Thinking about my best form or being the best player in the world doesn't mean anything to me."
For Bellingham, the ability to respond when things are not going according to plan is what separates the best teams from the rest.
"We're managing to show that mentality that good teams do, that even if you're not playing well, you can raise the level at any point," he said.
His adaptation to life in Spain has also been an important part of that journey.
Asked about his increasingly impressive Spanish, Bellingham admitted he still gets nervous when speaking the language in public.
"It's getting a little bit better. I get a little bit nervous speaking to you guys. It's much easier in the changing room," he joked to journalists.

"I'm loving living in Spain. I'm loving the club. I think for English players it's such an important thing to go and move abroad and learn new things and I've obviously benefited massively from that."
And while his performances have inevitably brought renewed attention to individual awards, Bellingham said that personal recognition is not what motivates him.
Asked about the Ballon d'Or, he said his focus was only on the team.
"I don't care about the Ballon d'Or, honestly. I want to win a lot of titles with the team, the Champions League, the League."
"The Ballon d'Or is something for you, journalists, to vote and create a bit of tension. But for me it's more important that the team win."

articles.headline: The difference between The Witcher 3 and Witcher 4 will be 'comparable' to that of GTA 5 and GTA 6, CD Projekt boss says: 'I mean, it's been 11 years'
keyFacts: CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski stated that The Witcher 4 will feature a technological leap comparable to the jump between GTA 5 and GTA 6.
Nowakowski said that the GTA 6 launch has not impacted PC sales or engagement for CD Projekt games.
The Witcher 4 is currently scheduled for release in 2028.
body: CD Projekt made its Q3 2026 financial report today, and there's not a whole lot to see: The Witcher 3 remaster was a big hit, work on Cyberpunk 2 and The Witcher 4 is ticking along, and everyone really liked Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.

Perhaps understandably, a number of questions in the subsequent investors call put the focus on Grand Theft Auto 6. While CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski didn't go too deep on the topic, he did say that the upcoming Witcher 4 will be comparable to GTA 6 in at least one way.

"Obviously, this is a call about us, not about Rockstar, but I do understand the connection here," Nowakowski said when asked if The Witcher 4 will represent a technological leap over its predecessor comparable to GTA 6. "Having said that, of course, I'm not going to make a deep dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course, we did look at the game. We did see the differences.

"Do we believe there's going to be a comparable leap between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4? I think so, yes. I mean, it's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game. So yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

Well, sure. As Nowakowski said, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was released 11 years ago, and it'll be two more years before The Witcher 4 comes out—assuming it's not delayed, which would make it a rarity among CD Projekt games. It will also be the same number of years between Witcher 3 and 4 as spanned GTA 5 and 6. In the world of technology, 13 years is a long time.
Hell, just the upgrade from the original Witcher 3 to the remastered version that dropped earlier this year is notable:

At the same time, Nowakowski said that while the GTA 6 launch was tremendously successful, CD Projekt Red doesn't intend to merely mimic Rockstar's approach when The Witcher 4 is ready to go: "Our games are different and the require a certain different approach, and we just do certain things differently than they do."
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

He also said that while the release of GTA 6 has had an impact on Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 sales on consoles, he doesn't expect it to have a "material impact" on the company's Q4 finances for one obvious reason.

"You do have to remember that a lot of our players are also PC-based," Nowakowski said. "GTA has not launched on PC. We have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales on engagement." And, he added, "on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero."

Nowakowsi also said that GTA 6 hasn't changed CD Projekt's ambitions for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2: If anything, it's "an inspiration in many ways for our developers." And he's not concerned about its success pushing up development budgets, because CD Projekt's games "are not budget-driven developments."

"I'm not saying that we don't care about the budgets. We do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well," Nowakowski said. "But you cannot make games like that having in mind, 'This is the fixed number of money I want to spend, and that's it. Otherwise, we're gone.'

"They are ambition-driven developments and money is important. The budgets are not indefinite. That's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is kind of like I said. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release. It has just always been like that."

Nowakowski's positive take on GTA 6 isn't too far off that of Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski, who said yesterday that he's suffering from "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression," although he quickly clarified that CD Projekt is "doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor." (And that he wasn't being serious about cancelling Cyberpunk 2.)

articles.headline: I'm not smart enough for the blocky, Factorio-esque spaceship and -station building sim Astario, but now that it's out in early access maybe you could be
keyFacts: The block-based spaceship and station building factory simulation game Astario launched into early access on Steam.
Players gather resources from asteroids and scrap to construct vehicles, orbital stations, and automated production machinery.
Players interested in the game can purchase it on Steam in early access now.
body: There are many different kinds of smarts, and the kind of smarts I am are absolutely zero help when it comes to games like Astario, a spaceship and space station building factory sim reminiscent of Factorio that just launched into early access. I think there's just so many moving parts in ways I can't wrap my head around, but I'm fairly confident that some of you will be, so I'll try to use the smarts I do have to tell you about it a bit more.

Astario puts you in a spaceship in, uh, space, and oh what a big space it is. I have no idea if it's a to scale universe or anything, but it certainly looks quite expansive. There is a Minecraftian quality to it in that you must fly about and find resources from things like asteroids and other bits of technological scrap, all of which is divided up into blocks. You can get quite granular with it, inspecting each individual cube up close to see if it's a material that you can make use of, adding it to your haul for use elsewhere.

As you acquire different kinds of blocks, be they functional or structural, you can build up various new vehicles and "create an imposing machine where all components work together to achieve your goal. Plan or design your build out of armor blocks, power supplies, life support components, tools, and production machinery. Construct an orbital station with a stash of cargo containers, or anchor your production base to an asteroid and turn its ores into more blocks, fully automatically. Equip your ship with docking ports for refueling or recharging." How you build things is up to you, you've seemingly got a lot of free reign in terms of artistic expression.

And then of course there's bits of production machinery you can produce that in turn net you recipes and the like so you can continue to improve your ship or space stations. "All production blocks have input and output ports that can be automated using logistic pipes which use request-based item routing," explains the game's Steam page of how techy you can get with it. "Simply hook up your inputs to a cargo container, and the machine will pull what it needs. Mining can be temporarily automated using specialized drills, which mine until the resources within its scope are depleted." If any of this sounds like it's up your alley, then you can pick up Astario on Steam in early access now.

articles.headline: How to change car plates in GTA 6
keyFacts: Players must reach Chapter Two and meet Moses Watkins at Watkins Auto Parts to unlock the ability to change vehicle license plates.

body: Stealing different vehicles and passing them off as your own is difficult in GTA 6. You can steal as many rides as you want, but you need to change your car’s license plate to keep it for yourself permanently.
You must progress the story slightly before you can swap plates. Here’s how to do it.
Table of contents
How to unlock license plate swaps in GTA 6
How to change car plates in GTA 6
How to unlock license plate swaps in GTA 6
The ability to change the license plate is locked in the early parts of the game. Once you’re in Chapter Two, Moses Watkins will ask you to bring him some cars, kicking off the process.
When you participate in the mission to find the cars, you’ll meet Moses at the Watkins Auto Parts in Port Gellhorn. Then, you’ll earn the Slim Jim tool, which allows you to steal cars.
Screenshot by Destructoid
Make sure you go and check out our sister site GTA 6 Bible for all your GTA 6 needs.
However, you’ll also unlock the feature to change the registration of vehicles by swapping their plates.
How to change car plates in GTA 6

You can only swap a car plate at Watkins Auto Parts. Moreover, you need to have an empty vehicle registration slot available, which may mean, unregistering one of your owned vehicles . Here’s a quick guide on how to do it:
First, steal the car. Initially, it’s better to opt for models that don’t have trackers.
Drive the car to Moses.
Press the L2/LT button to access the services offered by Moses.
Decide if you want to repaint the car.
Select the Register option, and the car plate will change due to a switch in ownership.
Eventually, you will learn how to do this with cars that have Advanced Trackers , allowing you to add the most valuable hypercars in Leonida to your garage.
